questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: identify the correct case for a direct object
questions.stem: In the sentence 'Ich sehe den Hund', which case does 'den Hund' take?

options.misconception: confuses the subject case with the object case
confuses the indirect object case with the direct object case
confuses the possessive case with the object case

questions.explanation: A direct object takes the accusative case, so 'den Hund' is accusative. The nominative marks the subject, the dative marks the indirect object, and the genitive marks possession, so each distractor names a real case applied to the wrong role.
questions.hint: Which case marks a direct object?

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: identify the dative case for an indirect object
questions.stem: In the sentence 'Ich gebe dem Kind ein Buch', which case does 'dem Kind' take?

options.misconception: confuses the direct object case with the indirect object case
confuses the subject case with the indirect object case
confuses the possessive case with the indirect object case

questions.explanation: 'dem Kind' is the indirect object and therefore takes the dative case. The accusative would mark the direct object, the nominative the subject, and the genitive possession.
questions.hint: Which case marks an indirect object?

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: identify the genitive case for possession
questions.stem: In the phrase 'Das Auto des Mannes', which case does 'des Mannes' take?

options.misconception: confuses the object case with the possessive case
confuses the subject case with the possessive case
confuses the indirect object case with the possessive case

questions.explanation: 'des Mannes' shows possession and takes the genitive case. The accusative marks a direct object, the nominative a subject, and the dative an indirect object.
questions.hint: Which case shows possession?

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: identify the nominative case for a subject
questions.stem: In the sentence 'Der Hund schlaeft', which case does 'Der Hund' take?

options.misconception: confuses the object case with the subject case
confuses the indirect object case with the subject case
confuses the possessive case with the subject case

questions.explanation: 'Der Hund' is the subject of the sentence and takes the nominative case. The accusative marks a direct object, the dative an indirect object, and the genitive possession.
questions.hint: Which case marks the subject?

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: conjugate a regular verb in the present tense
questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct present-tense form of 'spielen' for 'wir'?

options.misconception: uses the du ending for a wir subject
uses the er/sie/es ending for a wir subject
uses a past-tense form instead of the present tense

questions.explanation: For 'wir', the regular present-tense ending is '-en', giving 'spielen'. The '-st' ending belongs to 'du', '-t' to 'er/sie/es', and 'spielten' is past tense.
questions.hint: What ending does 'wir' take in the present tense?

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct form of 'sein' for 'ihr' (you plural)?

options.misconception: uses the sie (they) form for an ihr subject
uses the ich form for an ihr subject
uses the er/sie/es form for an ihr subject

questions.explanation: 'ihr' (you plural) takes 'seid' in the present tense. 'sind' is for 'sie' (they), 'bin' for 'ich', and 'ist' for 'er/sie/es'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct form of 'haben' for 'sie' (she)?

questions.explanation: 'sie' (she) takes 'hat' in the present tense. 'haben' is for 'sie' (they), 'hast' for 'du', and 'habt' for 'ihr'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct present-tense form of 'fahren' for 'er'?

options.misconception: omits the stem vowel change

uses a past-tense form instead of the present tense

questions.explanation: 'fahren' changes 'a' to 'ae' for 'er/sie/es', giving 'faehrt'. 'fahrt' keeps the wrong vowel, 'fahren' is the infinitive, and 'fuhr' is past tense.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct present-tense form of 'koennen' for 'ich'?

questions.explanation: 'ich' takes 'kann' with the modal verb 'koennen'. 'kannst' is for 'du', 'konnten' is past tense plural, and 'kanns' is not a valid form.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct Perfekt auxiliary for 'gehen'?

options.misconception: uses haben instead of sein for a motion verb
uses a past-perfect auxiliary form
uses the wrong auxiliary and tense

questions.explanation: Motion verbs such as 'gehen' form the Perfekt with 'sein', giving 'Ich bin gegangen'. 'haben' is for most other verbs, while 'war' and 'hatte' belong to the past perfect.

questions.learningObjective: select the correct definite article for a noun gender

options.misconception: uses the feminine article for a masculine noun
uses the neuter article for a masculine noun
uses an accusative form instead of the nominative

questions.explanation: 'Tisch' is masculine, so the nominative definite article is 'der'. 'die' is feminine, 'das' is neuter, and 'den' is the accusative masculine form.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct definite article for a plural noun?

options.misconception: uses the masculine singular article for a plural noun
uses the neuter singular article for a plural noun
uses an accusative form instead of the plural nominative

questions.explanation: The definite article for plural nouns in the nominative is 'die'. 'der', 'das', and 'den' are singular or case-specific forms and do not fit a plural subject.

questions.learningObjective: recognize a plural subject in a sentence
questions.stem: Which sentence has a plural subject?

options.misconception: chooses a singular subject instead of a plural one
chooses a singular subject instead of a plural one
chooses a singular subject instead of a plural one

questions.explanation: 'Die Hunde' is plural, while 'Der Hund', 'Das Kind', and 'Ein Vogel' are singular subjects. The plural subject also matches the plural verb 'bellen'.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: apply adjective declension after a definite article
questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct adjective ending after 'der' in the nominative masculine?

options.misconception: uses the dative or genitive ending in the nominative
uses the neuter ending for a masculine noun
uses the strong-declension ending after a definite article

questions.explanation: After 'der' in the nominative masculine, the weak adjective ending is '-e', giving 'alte'. 'alten' is dative/genitive, 'altes' is neuter, and 'alter' is strong declension without an article.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: choose the case after a two-way preposition with movement
questions.stem: Which case follows a two-way preposition when movement is involved?

options.misconception: confuses the stationary meaning with the movement meaning
confuses the subject case with a prepositional object
confuses the possessive case with a prepositional object

questions.explanation: Two-way prepositions such as 'in' and 'auf' take the accusative when the sentence expresses movement toward a destination. They take the dative when the location is stationary.
questions.hint: Does movement usually take accusative or dative?

names the object instead of the governing preposition
names the subject instead of the governing preposition

questions.explanation: 'mit' is the preposition that governs the dative case. 'dem' shows the dative form, 'Bus' is the object, and 'Ich' is the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses correct German word order?

places the subject after the object phrase
places the time phrase after the verb phrase

questions.explanation: In a main clause, the conjugated verb must occupy the second position, so 'Morgen gehe ich ins Kino' is correct. The other options violate verb-second order.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: place the verb at the end of a subordinate clause
questions.stem: Which sentence uses correct word order in a subordinate clause?

options.text: Ich weiss, dass er morgen kommt.
Ich weiss, dass er kommt morgen.

questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause introduced by 'dass', the conjugated verb must appear at the end, so 'dass er morgen kommt' is correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 'kein' correctly?

uses a dative form instead of the nominative

questions.explanation: 'kein' negates a noun and must agree in gender and number, so 'kein Auto' is correct. 'nicht' negates verbs or adjectives, 'keine' is feminine or plural, and 'keinem' is dative.

questions.explanation: In a main clause, the prefix 'auf' moves to the end, giving 'Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf'. The other options leave the verb unsplit or misplace the prefix.
